contexts.text: They lived in friendship, civility, etc.

By islands, they perceive those things within the Church which are a little further removed from charity, as are friendships, and civilities; friendship is not charity, still less is civility, but they are a degree below charity; but the more they derive from charity, the more sound they are.
They are dismissed with civility and charity.
Knowledges... are everything scientific... with which he can be imbued from civil life, from doctrine, and from the Word.
As to the perception of what is just and fair in civil life...
As to civil life, they live in what is just and fair...
Man is led by the Lord through almost the same things in spiritual life, as those through which man leads others in civil life...
They separate spiritual life from civil to such a degree...
Perceiving what is honest in moral life, what is just in civil life, and what is good in spiritual life.
Life according to the laws of what is just and honest, without spiritual life, is civil and moral life; this life causes a man to be a citizen of the world, the former, a citizen of Heaven.
In externals they appeared modest, civil, etc.
The truths of the civil state, which are of what is just...

Judgments = exterior truths, such as there must be in the civil state, where there is a representative Church... Judgments, in the plural, = the civil laws... Things of life are called precepts, things of the civil state, judgments... AC 9857:10.
To Divine good natural pertains also civil good, which is called what is just among the citizens.
There are two things with men which must be in order, the things of Heaven, and the things of the world; those of Heaven are called ecclesiastical things, those of the world, civil things. NJHD 311.
In the Heavens there are... ecclesiastical, civil, and domestic affairs...

In civil affairs are those (in Heaven) who in this world had loved their country and its common good in preference to their own, and who had done what is just and right from the love of what is just and right...
From civil and pretended friendship...
Truths are of three kinds: civil, moral, and spiritual. Civil truths relate to those things which are of judgment and of government in kingdoms; in general, to what is just and equitable therein.

There are three degrees of life with every man: the Rational is opened to the first degree through civil truths... not by merely knowing them, but by living according to them; that is, loving them from spiritual affection. Explained.
[Swedenborg footnote 1.] Civil good, which is what is just, is the neighbour.
What is just and fair is of civil life.
In the four following commandments are delivered the laws of civil life.
On ecclesiastical and civil government. General article. (From AC 10789, et seq.)

There are civil good, moral good, and spiritual good: civil good is that which man does from the civil law; through this good and according to it is man a citizen in the natural world... Civil good is the ultimate.
The man who has spiritual good is a moral man and also a civil man; but the man who has not spiritual good appears to be a moral and civil man, but is not. Explained.

It is from this that he is able to become a civil and moral man; and he who is a civil and moral man can also become spiritual, for the civil and moral is the receptacle of the Spiritual. He is called a civil man who knows the laws of the kingdom wherein he is a citizen, and lives according to them... Live these laws, not only as civil and moral laws, but also as Divine laws, and you will be a spiritual man... The civil and moral man keeps these laws, that he may be, or may seem to be, a good citizen; but if he does not at the same time regard these laws as Divine, he is only a natural civil and moral man; whereas, if he also regards them as Divine, he becomes a spiritual civil and moral man. Further Explained.
The universal judgment... upon those who had been in civil and moral good, and in no spiritual good. Signified.
He commanded... to show them all the honours of civility.
The sex is then treated with civil morality.

The things which belong to the common weal, and are called civil, hold a place below these spiritual things... because they conjoin themselves with the world, for they are of the world; for statutes, laws, and rules are what bind men...
(Politeness one of the moral virtues.)
Varieties of similitudes... can be conjoined... through civilities, etc.
Of these polygamists they are saved who acknowledge God, and, from religion, live according to the civil laws of justice. Explained.
I saw many gathered together... some... of the ecclesiastical order, some... of the civil order; all of whom were learned...
Food, clothing, and many other things which there are in civil life...
The natural (necessities of our country) regard civil life and order.
By his country man is initiated into civil life; by the Church into spiritual life... Civil life is temporary...
These spiritual things... remain with man; but not in like manner civil and political things... because civil and political things, being of the world, reside in the lower parts of the mind...

Theological matters... then remain only in the understanding in the political things which have relation to his own life... in the civil things which belong to his employment, and in the domestic things which are of his house...
The things of the natural world, which are called civil and moral...
Religion... sees beneath itself the civil things which are of the world.
The Christian as the heathen... does the goods of civility and of morality to his companion.
On the civil state.

There are some in the other life who live in a so-called civil state... When any Spirit comes who is not good, they speak civilly to him... hence the Spirit too is reduced into a civil state... It is not a pretended state, but is sincere, for they speak through civil things...
On civil society in the other life.

There, are a number of Societies which are civil Societies; so are they to be called; who show civility to everyone, not so much from the heart as from the lips, though still not entertaining anything evil or false in their hearts; as when they say to a guest that his coming is grateful and acceptable... Not lying with the intention to deceive or do evil, but because they have been accustomed to speak so in the bodily life... They are good Spirits... It was given me to say that it was all the same so to speak when there was nothing of evil in it...
Thus no spiritual life; but only natural and civil life...
They believed they would come into Heaven, because in externals they had lived morally and civilly... But now they notice that civil life is a different thing from spiritual life.
Spiritual, civil, moral, and natural. Explained.
5. 2. Civil truths are the civil laws of kingdoms and cities...
Civil good is the good of life according to civil laws... If in this good there is not moral good, and in this spiritual good, it is no other good than the animal good in which are beasts...
Through civil good a man is a man of the world...
